Class ExecutionContext

java.lang.Object
io.github.kaivian.klibrary.context.ExecutionContext
public final class ExecutionContext extends Object
Shared execution context passed to all actions and requirements.

The ExecutionContext encapsulates all contextual information needed during action execution or requirement evaluation. It provides access to the target player, the command sender, custom placeholders, arbitrary metadata, and the owning plugin (needed for scheduling, etc.).

Instances are created via the ExecutionContext.Builder:

ExecutionContext context = ExecutionContext.builder()
    .player(player)
    .sender(player)
    .plugin(myPlugin)
    .placeholder("reward", "100")
    .metadata("source", "daily_quest")
    .build();

The context is immutable after construction. Placeholder and metadata maps are wrapped as unmodifiable views.

  • Method Details

    • getPlayer

      public Optional<org.bukkit.entity.Player> getPlayer()
      Returns the target player for this execution, if present.

      May be empty for console-only contexts (e.g., broadcast actions triggered from the console without a player target).

      Returns:
      an Optional containing the player, or empty

    • getSender

      public org.bukkit.command.CommandSender getSender()
      Returns the command sender for this execution.

      If no explicit sender was set, this defaults to the player. Will be null only if neither player nor sender was provided.

      Returns:
      the command sender, or null if none was set

    • getPlugin

      public Optional<org.bukkit.plugin.Plugin> getPlugin()
      Returns the owning plugin for this execution.

      This is used by actions that need to schedule tasks (e.g., DelayAction) or access plugin-specific resources.

      Returns:
      an Optional containing the plugin, or empty if not set

    • getPlaceholders

      public Map<String,String> getPlaceholders()
      Returns the custom placeholder map for this execution.

      These placeholders are applied in addition to PlaceholderAPI placeholders (if available). Custom placeholders use the format {key} and are resolved before MiniMessage parsing.

      Returns:
      an unmodifiable map of placeholder key-value pairs

    • getMetadata

      public Map<String,Object> getMetadata()
      Returns the metadata map for this execution.

      Metadata provides an extensible way to pass arbitrary data through the execution pipeline. External plugins can use this to attach custom state to action/requirement evaluations.

      Returns:
      an unmodifiable map of metadata key-value pairs
